question.title: How many New World screwworm cases will be confirmed in Mexico in total before July 2027?
question.description:
[New World screwworm](https://www.cdc.gov/new-world-screwworm/about/index.html) (NWS) is species of parasitic fly that completes part of its lifecycle by feeding on the tissue or flesh of warm-blooded animals, including humans. NWS is typically found in South America and parts of the Caribbean, but since 2023 the fly has steadily moved northward from South America through every country in Central America and into Mexico. NWS can be particularly devastating to livestock health, causing serious economic impacts.

The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) currently disperses 100 million sterile insects per week in Mexico and closely evaluates the location and circumstances of each new case to adjust sterile-insect release efforts and locations as needed.

Through April 15, 2026, there were a total of 20,591 confirmed animal cases of [NWS in Mexico](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1), with 1,295 active cases.
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases of New World screwworm in Mexico before July 1, 2027, according to the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) [Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service current status report](https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/stop-screwworm/current-status?page=1), rounded to the nearest 500.
question.fine_print:
The map and list of cases is updated on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 5:00 p.m. ET by the USDA. This question will resolve as the total number of animal cases on the latest report before July 1, 2027, provided this is published at the earliest by June 1, 2027.

If the USDA ceases reporting or significantly changes its criteria such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**.
